properties.decision:
Take rmcp 3.0.1 on Anthony's direct word ("I want to upgrade to rmcp v3.0.1"), replacing the `rmcp = "2"` pin. The entire code change is one generic bound in `serve_http`: rmcp v3 narrowed `StreamableHttpService::new` from `S: Service<RoleServer>` to `S: ServerHandler`, because the sessionless transport builds a handler per REQUEST and must ask it for `get_info` and the tool list with no session having cached them. Both surfaces that come through that door — the real service and the degraded one — already implement `ServerHandler` via `#[tool_handler]`, so nothing was lost.

NOT chosen: staying on rmcp 2 until the seat question is answered. The upgrade and the seat fix are separable, and holding a working dependency bump hostage to an open design decision would have left reflow2 on a pinned major with no evidence about what actually breaks.
properties.name: Upgrade to rmcp 3.0.1 now, as a one-line bound change, and measure what it costs rather than reasoning about it
properties.rationale:
The v3.0.0 notes list eight breaking-change areas — sessionless Streamable HTTP, stateless lifecycle, subscriptions, MRTR response enums on `call_tool`/`get_prompt`/`read_resource`, the tasks API, split metadata types, OAuth, MSRV 1.88 — and exactly one of them reached reflow2's code. The `#[tool]`/`#[tool_router]`/`#[tool_handler]` macros absorbed the MRTR enum change entirely, MSRV 1.88 is under this workspace's 1.94, and the OAuth, tasks and subscription surfaces are ones reflow2 never touched. All 118 toolsnaps match, so the served tool surface did not move.

THE PART THAT MATTERED WAS NOT IN THE DIFF. Every gate stayed green, and that green was misleading: every one of reflow2's own test clients negotiates `2025-06-18`, `2025-11-25` or `2024-11-05`, and `ProtocolVersion::LATEST` in rmcp 3.0.1 is still `V_2025_11_25`. Nothing in the suite speaks `2026-07-28`, so nothing exercised the sessionless path that the whole requirement is about. This is the same failure shape as row 3AX-3 in the coverage matrix the day before: a green tick only as wide as the case its evidence exercises.

Measured instead, with `tools/stateless_seat_probe.py` — one client, two `claim_region` calls, count the distinct seats. stdio: one seat. HTTP at 2025-06-18: one seat. HTTP at 2026-07-28: TWO seats, one per request. So `req:seat-per-client` is intact on every transport in use today and broken on exactly one that nothing uses yet, which is why this is a deadline and not an outage — Claude Code and grok build both connect over stdio.

There is no configuration that avoids it: `StreamableHttpServerConfig::legacy_session_mode` is documented to apply only to protocol versions below 2026-07-28, and requests negotiating that version "are always served statelessly regardless of this setting". The CLIENT chooses the version, so reflow2 cannot decline on its behalf; it can only decide what identity means once the choice is made.
